Subject: Deployment mode recap & next steps (HIPAA/BAA/SOC2)

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move toward a pilot decision: 

Summary of deployment-mode options (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to production. We can sign a BAA and configure logging/retention settings, but note that hosted multi-tenant endpoints have shared infrastructure. For production PHI workloads we typically recommend either Dedicated or Private for added isolation and SLA/throughput guarantees.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): dedicated GPU pools with predictable throughput, tenant isolation, and ability to enforce stricter network controls. Good balance for customers who want isolation without managing infra.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer-managed networking, suitable for regulated or air-gapped workflows where you control the environment and KMS.

Security/compliance asks you raised: HIPAA/BAA, SOC 2 evidence, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data residency, and evidence of access controls.

Attachments I’m sending now: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (SOC 2 Type II summary) and Redwood_BAA_Template.docx. I’ve also attached a short mutual action plan (Redwood_MAP_Elara_Health_20270315.pdf) with suggested milestones (BAA signature, security deep-dive, pilot window).

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Elara will send PHI to Redwood for the pilot (yes/no).
2) Sign the BAA (we can iterate) — I’ve attached our template.
3) Complete the security questionnaire where helpful (Dylan can help with any technical answers).
4) Schedule a 60-minute security deep-dive with our security engineering team next week to walk SOC2 controls, logging, KMS options, and deployment topologies.

Can you confirm which deployment mode Elara is leaning toward and share expected QPS / concurrency and peak tokens per request so we can give a sizing/pricing snapshot?

Thanks — I’ll hold a slot for a security call next Wed/Thu afternoon PT unless you prefer different times.

—
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Deployment mode for HIPAA workloads — next steps & SOC 2 evidence

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before the security call: 

1) PHI scope: yes, the pilot will include limited PHI (deidentified-by-default is not possible for this use case). We need guarantees on data handling and auditability.
2) Evidence we need before pilot kickoff:
   - SOC 2 Type II report (latest)
   - Executed BAA (will need some custom language around subprocessors and data retention)
   - Confirmation of audit log retention and access controls (who can see logs, how long retained)
   - Encryption at rest and in transit; support for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) if we go Dedicated or Private
   - Data residency: US-only.
3) Deployment preference: Elara is currently leaning toward Dedicated capacity for predictable performance, but we need pricing ballpark and what isolation guarantees Dedicated provides vs Hosted. If Dedicated doesn’t meet our requirements we’ll request Private VPC.

Also please send any sample MAP and an estimated timeline for signing BAA + security review. We’d like to aim for a pilot start in mid-April if possible.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Product & Security | Elara Health

Subject: Re: Deployment mode for HIPAA workloads — next steps & SOC 2 evidence

Thanks Samir — good notes. Answering inline and adding next steps: 

On PHI scope: understood — pilot with PHI is fine but will require an executed BAA and a security kickoff prior to ingest.

Evidence we can provide (see attached):
- SOC 2 Type II summary + controls: attached Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (full report available under NDA).
- BAA: attached Redwood_BAA_Template.docx — happy to review any redlines; note we list subprocessors and provide a signature block.
- Audit logs & retention: Redwood stores request/response metadata and operational logs. We retain audit logs for 12 months by default for Dedicated customers; retention can be extended on request (and we can discuss S3 export of logs to Elara-controlled bucket). Access to logs is role-based — only authorized SecOps and account engineers have viewing rights; we can provide a summarized access matrix in the security call.
- Encryption/KMS: For Dedicated and Private, we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS / external HSM). Hosted can use platform-managed keys; we can restrict export and minimize retention configuration for Hosted but customer-managed KMS requires Dedicated or Private.
- Data residency: we can ensure US-only region placement for Dedicated or Private.

Deployment recommendation: Given you need PHI + predictable latency, Dedicated is the recommended starting point: gives tenant-level isolation, dedicated GPU pools, and supports customer KMS and US-only placement. Private VPC is available if Elara requires control of network egress or an on-prem option.

Sizing / pricing: to give a quick ballpark I need expected concurrent requests / peak tokens. If you’re targeting ~50 concurrent users with small-to-medium token sizes, we can propose a quarterly Dedicated commit. I’ve attached a one-page MAP (Redwood_MAP_Elara_Health_20270315.pdf) with milestones and an estimated 6–8 week pilot timeline (including BAA and security review).

Next actions I’ll take this week:
- Send SOC2 + BAA (done, attachments).
- Schedule security deep-dive — Dylan, can you take lead on the call and be ready to go through audit logs, KMS, and network topology?

Samir / Priya — could you confirm:
- PHI = yes (confirmed)
- Target pilot start = mid-April (are you ok with 2027-04-18 start?)

If you confirm those two items I’ll put together a draft SOW and a Dedicated sizing/pricing snapshot for review.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
